title: `structure()` calls cause deprecation warnings in R-devel
description:
[My package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=covidcast) recently got a notification that its tests are failing on CRAN and it'll be removed on August 21 if they're not fixed. When I got a test environment set up, I found the problem is in httptest:

```
Warning (test-covidcast.R:81:5): covidcast_signal warns when requested geo_values are unavailable
Replacing special names '.Names' is deprecated; use 'names' instead.
Backtrace:
     ▆
  1. ├─testthat::expect_warning(...) at test-covidcast.R:81:5
  2. │ └─testthat:::expect_condition_matching_(...)
  3. │   └─testthat:::quasi_capture(...)
  4. │     ├─testthat (local) .capture(...)
  5. │     │ └─base::withCallingHandlers(...)
  6. │     └─rlang::eval_bare(quo_get_expr(.quo), quo_get_env(.quo))
  7. └─covidcast::covidcast_signal(...)
  8.   └─covidcast:::covidcast_days(...) at covidcast/R/covidcast.R:321:3
  9.     └─covidcast:::covidcast(...) at covidcast/R/covidcast.R:823:5
 10.       └─covidcast:::.request("covidcast", params) at covidcast/R/covidcast.R:995:3
 11.         └─httr::GET(url, user_agent, headers, query = params) at covidcast/R/covidcast.R:1057:3
 12.           └─httr:::request_perform(req, hu$handle$handle)
 13.             └─httr:::request_fetch(req$output, req$url, handle)
 14.               └─httptest (local) `<fn>`(req)
 15.                 └─httptest:::load_response(mockfile, req)
 16.                   └─httptest::fake_response(...)
 17.                     ├─base::structure(...)
 18.                     └─base::structure(...)
 19.                       └─base::.Deprecated(...)

Failure (test-covidcast.R:87:5): covidcast_signal warns when requested geo_values are unavailable
Expected `suppressMessages(...)` to run silently.
Actual noise: warnings.
 ```

The `structure()` documentation in R-devel says:

```
     The historical feature to rename attributes ‘".Dim"’,
     ‘".Dimnames"’, ‘".Names"’, ‘".Tsp"’ and ‘".Label"’ is deprecated
     since R version 4.7.0.
```

I see you have a similar NOTE on the [httptest check results](https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_httptest.html); in my case it's a warning instead of a note because it's in a test using `expect_silent()`.

I think the fix is as simple as looking at all the places using `.Names` in `structure()` and replacing the argument name with `names`; you can find those places in a search: https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Anealrichardson%2Fhttptest+%22.Names%22&type=code

Happy to make a PR doing this if it'd help get a release out. Of course I can probably hack around it in my tests to appease CRAN, but since this will affect others using httptest, happy to put the effort in here instead.

title: safe_untrace() can NOT work with a function object as argument, nor with a scoped function name
description:
`safe_untrace()` silently (because of the try()) fails,  if given a function as argument:

```
# as in stop_mocking()
safe_untrace(curl::form_file)
```
This can not work since:
- what == curl::form_file, a function
- `get(what, env)` - requires a character first argument
It silently fails because of the `try(, silent = TRUE)`.

Also, it could not work with `safe_untrace("curl::form_file")` since get() does not understand scoped function names.
Instead, it should be called like:
```
>safe_untrace('form_file', where = getNamespace('curl'))
Untracing function "form_file" in package "namespace:curl"
[1] "form_file"
```
It is partially responsible for #66 .


For reference:

```
safe_untrace <- function(what, where = sys.frame()) {
  # If you attempt to untrace a function (1) that isn't exported from
  # whatever namespace it lives in and (2) that isn't currently traced,
  # it errors. This prevents that so that it's always safe to call `untrace`

  # untrace() and get() handle enviroments differently
  if (is.environment(where)) {
    env <- where
  } else {
    env <- environment(where)
  }
  if (inherits(try(get(what, env), silent = TRUE), "functionWithTrace")) {
    quietly(untrace(what, where = where))
  }
}
```

title: Using httptest in vignettes: How to make sure that recorded requests are actually used when building the package?
description:
Thanks a lot for your great work on this package.

I'm using httptest in the vignette for a package that interacts with an API. The API credentials are stored in my `.renviron` file. I am using the process as described in the ["Vignettes" vignette](https://enpiar.com/r/httptest/articles/vignettes.html). After building the vignette locally, I also have the expected folders and file names on my computer that should then be used by httptest in the vignette.

However, it seems that httptest ignores the recorded requests. This is most obvious when building a source package and checking it on another machine, which leads to the following warning.

```
* checking re-building of vignette outputs ... WARNING
Error(s) in re-building vignettes:
```

title: Add documentation on how to test for error behavior
description:
Writing down what I think I understood

* [Your blog post](https://enpiar.com/2017/06/21/7-hard-testing-problems-made-easy-by-httptest/#5-rare-or-difficult-to-trigger-server-behavior). How exactly did you create https://github.com/Crunch-io/rcrunch/blob/d1b5cade5e7b0608ddc1ce5de1a576e2d3614d84/tests/testthat/app.crunch.io/503.R? I.e. what did you have to guess?

* Use `capture_requests(, simplify = FALSE)` with a call that works. This way you get a fixture with the right filepath, and with all fields. Edit the fixture, replace `capture_request()` with `with_mock_api()`. (that's what I did).

* To guess the filepath, the easiest solution is otherwise to run the test with `with_mock_api` when the mock file doesn't exist, because the error message contains the mock filepath. (this is explained in the blog post)

* Mocking httr functions https://github.com/cran/datapackage.r/blob/0bc1caa1903cf36b2d5f318265426eb072c361d7/tests/testthat/test-profile.R#L68 that's closer to what webmockr would let one do, actually. I.e. not writing the fake to file.

In all cases a good package structure seems to help, e.g. in your blog post example having `crGET()` makes things easier.
Also, if one wants to test the exact same function calls in two situations (server up, server down), one might need to play with .mockPaths().

description:
